newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenya shilling weaker vs dlr in uneasy market.
newsitem.headline: Kenya shilling weaker vs dlr in uneasy market.

text.p: The Kenyan shilling extended losses against the dollar in a market uneasy of political unrest, commercial bank dealers said.
The Central Bank of Kenya posted a shilling mean rate of 58.78 against the dollar from 58.10 on Monday and a mean of 99.27 versus the pound from 98.30 on Monday.
Dealers said although the alarming levels of demand seen last Thursday and Friday had eased, they were still trading cautiously.
"The market still remains nervous and spreads are wide. Everyone's cautious just in case the buy demand comes in again," a senior dealer said.
Political unrest, the worst in seven years, sparked panic and triggered a surge in dollar demand that drove the shilling down to as low as 61.50.

Nine people were killed last week after riot police dispersed rallies called by Kenya's opposition movement to press for minimal constitutional reforms before general elections. No date has been fixed for the elections.
Leading business figures have urged the government and the opposition to seek dialogue as a solution to the crisis.
Central bank intervention on Friday helped the shilling recoup some of its heavy losses.
Dealers said they expected the shilling to continue trade nervously until they received signals from foreign investors that they were not alarmed about the political climate.
"Right now, everyone is just sitting on the sides. Foreign investors are still concerned. They keep calling to find out about the situation here," a dealer said.
The central bank said it was not against gradual and orderly depreciation of the shilling based on economic fundamentals.

"However, rapid fluctuations in the shilling exchange rate due to non-economic factors is a cause for concern as such behaviour erodes investor confidence," Maurice Kanga, central bank chief economist, said in a statement.
The money market eased on an inflow of funds from last week's treasury bill auction.
Overnight rates were quoted at between 10-13 percent compared to 20-23 percent on Monday.
